knowledge:
- key_parameters: Enrichment_Analysis=Logical determining whether to perform pathway enrichment analysis (default FALSE) ;; Contextual_Analysis=Logical determining whether to perform contextual association analysis between pathways (default FALSE) ;; DirectEvidence_info=A matrix where the first column contains NCBI Entrez Gene IDs and subsequent columns contain direct evidence values (e.g., negative log10 transformed p-values) ;; Adjacency=A square adjacency matrix representing gene connectivity in the pooled pathway ;; pathway=A dataframe representing edges in the pooled pathway with columns for connected gene IDs and pathway titles ;; Column_DirectEvidence=Integer specifying the column index in DirectEvidence_info containing the direct evidence of interest ;; n_perm=Number of permutations for significance testing (default 2000) ;; threshold=p-value cutoff used to identify differentially expressed genes (default 0.05) ;; use_sig_pathways=Logical indicating whether to restrict contextual analysis only to pathways identified as significant in enrichment analysis (default FALSE)
- alternatives: Standard hypergeometric test (calculated and outputted alongside PathNet results as p_Hyper) ;; alternative statistical tests (e.g., ANOVA, SAM) can be used to generate the input p-values instead of a t-test
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing transcriptomic data (e.g., microarray or RNA-seq converted to gene-level p-values) and you want to incorporate pathway topology (neighboring gene interactions) and pathway cross-talk (contextual association) rather than treating pathways as simple independent gene sets
- pitfalls: DirectEvidence_info must be provided and its first column must always contain the NCBI Entrez Gene IDs, otherwise the program will fail ;; Indirect evidence is only calculated for genes present in the KEGG pathway with at least one edge (others will be NA and combined evidence will default to direct evidence) ;; Running contextual analysis with use_sig_pathways = FALSE on all pathways is computationally intensive and can take several hours

workflows.name: pathway_enrichment_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify significantly enriched pathways by combining direct gene expression evidence with pathway topological neighbor information.
input: brain_regions_data.txt (matrix of gene IDs and direct evidence p-values)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the direct evidence, adjacency matrix, and pathway data ;; 2. Filter the adjacency matrix to match the gene IDs present in the direct evidence ;; 3. Run the PathNet function with Enrichment_Analysis set to TRUE ;; 4. Retrieve enrichment results and combined evidence from the output list
workflows.code:
library("PathNet")
library("PathNetData")
data(brain_regions)
data(A)
gene_ID <- brain_regions[,1]
A <- A [rownames(A) %in% gene_ID, rownames(A) %in% gene_ID]
data(pathway)
results <- PathNet(Enrichment_Analysis = TRUE, 
        DirectEvidence_info = brain_regions[1:2000,], 
        Adjacency = A, 
        pathway = pathway, 
        Column_DirectEvidence = 7,
        n_perm = 10, threshold = 0.05) 
results$enrichment_results[1:10,]
results$enrichment_combined_evidence[1:10,]

workflows.name: pathway_contextual_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify pathway contextual associations and overlap scores to find biologically related pathways based on the connectivity of differentially expressed genes.
input: brain_regions_data.txt (matrix of gene IDs and direct evidence p-values)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the direct evidence, adjacency matrix, and pathway data ;; 2. Filter the adjacency matrix to match the gene IDs present in the direct evidence ;; 3. Run the PathNet function with Contextual_Analysis set to TRUE ;; 4. Retrieve the contextual association p-values and pathway overlap scores from the output list
workflows.code:
library("PathNet")
library("PathNetData")
data(brain_regions)
data(A)
gene_ID <- brain_regions[,1]
A <- A [rownames(A) %in% gene_ID, rownames(A) %in% gene_ID]
data(pathway)
results <- PathNet(Enrichment_Analysis = FALSE, 
        Contextual_Analysis= TRUE, 
        DirectEvidence_info = brain_regions[1:500,], 
        Adjacency = A, 
        pathway = pathway, 
        Column_DirectEvidence = 7, 
        use_sig_pathways = FALSE, 
        n_perm = 10, threshold = 0.05)
results$conn_p_value[1:4, 1:2]
results$pathway_overlap[1:4, 1:2]
